24238.title: Sketcher: Trim does not work with an external line and a circle
24238.feasibility_reason: The issue is confirmed and described with a sample file and screenshots, making it reproducible. However, debugging geometric trim algorithms in FreeCAD's Sketcher workbench involving external geometry (reference geometry) requires understanding OCC and Sketcher intersection logic.
24238.problem_summary: Sketcher's trim tool removes an entire circle instead of cutting it at intersections with external geometry lines.
24238.root_cause_hypothesis: The intersection calculation logic in the Sketcher trim command only considers normal/internal sketch geometry (positive geometry indices) and ignores or skips external geometry elements (stored separately or indexed with negative IDs), causing the trim algorithm to detect zero intersection points and delete the entire circle.
24238.suggested_approach: Include external geometry curves when finding intersections for the curve being trimmed, ensuring intersection points can be computed with projected external lines/curves while ensuring the external geometry itself remains unmodified.
prerequisites: Local FreeCAD build environment with Sketcher module enabled
Understanding of SketchObject internal vs. external geometry representations and GeoEnum indexing
implementation_steps: Inspect the trim tool implementation (search for `trim` methods in `SketchObject` and `CommandSketcherTools`) to locate where intersection points with candidate cutting geometries are computed.

Examine how candidate intersecting curves are collected: determine whether the iteration is restricted to `sketch->getGeometry()` without considering `sketch->getExternalGeometry()` / negative indices.
Update the intersection gathering logic to also include external geometries (or projected curves of external geometry) as potential cutting entities.
Ensure intersection points against bounded external geometry (e.g., line segments) properly check parameter bounds / tolerance.

Handle constraint creation or endpoint positioning when splitting a circle into an arc so that point-on-object or coincidence constraints with the external geometry work properly if auto-constraints are enabled.
Verify that trimming an external curve directly is still disallowed or prevented, and only normal geometries are modified/trimmed.
Add automated or manual regression tests verifying trimming circles, arcs, and lines against external geometry lines and curves.

27762.problem_summary: Several widgets and controls on the Part/PartDesign 'General' preferences page in FreeCAD lack descriptive tooltips, making options unclear to users.
27762.root_cause_hypothesis: The Qt Designer UI definition file (.ui) for the Part/PartDesign General preferences page does not have the 'toolTip' property defined for several input widgets and checkboxes.
27762.suggested_approach: Locate the UI file corresponding to the Part/PartDesign General preferences page, identify all controls/checkboxes/inputs lacking tooltips, and add clear, descriptive tooltip text directly in Qt Designer or the .ui XML definition.

Qt Designer or a text editor to modify Qt .ui XML files
Understanding of Part and PartDesign workbench preferences and their functionality

Inspect the UI file in Qt Designer or XML editor and compare against the settings shown under Edit -> Preferences -> Part/PartDesign -> General.

Add the `<property name="toolTip"><string>...</string></property>` entries to the respective widgets in the UI file.

Ensure translation strings are properly marked/formatted according to FreeCAD's UI standards and submit a pull request.

19709.title: Measurement: Error when clicking on measure label only on DXF import
19709.feasibility_reason: The issue provides clear reproduction steps and a stack trace indicating a segmentation fault in Gui::SoFCUnifiedSelection::setSelection when clicking a measure label on a DXF import. However, debugging GUI selection handlers and the interaction with imported DXF geometry might require some familiarity with FreeCAD's Inventor/Coin3D integration and selection mechanisms.
19709.problem_summary: FreeCAD crashes with a segmentation fault in Gui::SoFCUnifiedSelection::setSelection when a user clicks on a measurement label in the 3D viewer.
19709.root_cause_hypothesis: When the user clicks on a 3D measurement label, the selection event is handled by SoFCUnifiedSelection. The picked path resolves to an internal measurement Coin node (or an object without a standard document object / selection adapter), and SoFCUnifiedSelection attempts to dereference null or invalid object pointers/metadata when processing the picked element, accompanied by the log 'No measure handler available for geometry of module: Measure'.
19709.suggested_approach: Add null checks and guard against picking non-selectable measurement scene graph nodes in SoFCUnifiedSelection::setSelection and SoFCUnifiedSelection::handleEvent, or ensure measurement label Coin nodes are explicitly marked non-pickable / non-selectable for standard document selection passes.
prerequisites: Build environment for FreeCAD with Coin3D, Qt, and Python bindings enabled.
A test DXF file or generic CAD model reproducing measurement creation in the Measure workbench.
implementation_steps: Reproduce the crash in a debug build by creating a measurement with the Measure tool and clicking directly on the resulting measurement label in the 3D viewport.

Inspect the stack frame in `Gui::SoFCUnifiedSelection::setSelection` and `handleEvent` to identify which pointer dereference or index lookup is causing the SIGSEGV when a measurement label node is picked.
Add null checks and valid-object validation in `SoFCUnifiedSelection` for picked paths that lack a backing `App::DocumentObject` or `Gui::ViewProvider`.
Check measurement Coin nodes (like text / dimension labels in `Mod/Measure`) and verify if their pick style should be set to `SoPickStyle::UNPICKABLE` or handled gracefully if selected.

Investigate and handle the warning 'No measure handler available for geometry of module: Measure' to ensure measurement entities do not recursively attempt to measure themselves or fail silently without crashing.
Test clicking measurement labels across different geometry types (DXF 2D shapes, 3D solids, empty space) to confirm the crash is eliminated and selection behaves as expected.

28930.title: Measurement: Length measured with `Std_Measure` is attached to geometric center, not midpoint
28930.feasibility_reason: The issue clearly identifies the problem and expected behavior in the measurement tool, but locating where the calculation uses the geometric center versus the curve midpoint requires navigating the C++ codebase of the Std_Measure tool.
28930.problem_summary: When measuring the length of a curved edge or spline with Std_Measure, the annotation label/dimension line anchor attaches to the geometric center (barycenter/bounding center) rather than the midpoint lying directly on the curve.
28930.root_cause_hypothesis: The measurement calculation for edge length queries the center of mass (e.g., via `BRepGProp` center of mass or bounding box center) or a similar centroid calculation instead of evaluating the point on the curve at parameter `(u_start + u_end) / 2` or at half of the edge's total arc length.
28930.suggested_approach: Update the point/placement calculation in the measurement code for edge length measurements to evaluate the point at the parametric midpoint or arc-length midpoint of the edge/curve using OpenCASCADE curve evaluation utilities (e.g. `BRepAdaptor_Curve` or `GCPnts_AbscissaPoint`), ensuring the annotation anchor sits directly on the curve.
prerequisites: Build FreeCAD from source with OpenCASCADE (OCC) development headers and Qt support enabled.
implementation_steps: Search the Measure module and Gui measurement commands for the calculation of the position/anchor point for length measurements of TopoDS_Edge and curve objects.
Identify where the barycenter or center of mass is currently computed (such as `GProp_GProps` / `BRepGProp::LinearProperties` or center point computation).

Modify the calculation for edge/curve length measurement to compute the curve's midpoint: retrieve the first and last curve parameters (or use arc length parameterization via `GCPnts_AbscissaPoint`), evaluate the 3D point at the midpoint parameter using OCC's `Value()` or `D0()` method.
Handle edge cases such as closed/periodic curves, zero-length edges, and trimmed curves properly.
Rebuild FreeCAD and verify using Std_Measure on various non-straight curves (splines, circles, arcs, ellipses, complex NURBS edges) to ensure annotations sit on the curve itself.
Run existing measurement unit and GUI tests to ensure no regressions for straight edge length or other measurement types.

While fixing tab orders in Qt UI files or Python/C++ dialogs is usually straightforward, identifying the exact file and widget hierarchy without prior codebase knowledge may take some investigation.
blockers: Locating the specific UI definition or code responsible for the Section Plane dialog/task panel
30833.problem_summary: Keyboard Tab/Shift-Tab navigation across input fields in TechDraw's Section Plane task panel follows an erratic, non-intuitive sequence.
30833.root_cause_hypothesis: The tab stop order in the Qt UI file (.ui) or programmatic `setTabOrder` chain for the Section Plane task panel widget was not explicitly configured, causing Qt to default to creation order or layout geometry which does not match the visual top-to-bottom / logical input sequence.
30833.suggested_approach: Inspect the Section Plane UI definition file in Qt Designer or code, define an explicit and intuitive tab order (tabstops) linking input fields from top to bottom and left to right, and verify focus behavior during keyboard navigation.
prerequisites: Working FreeCAD development environment with Qt6/Qt5 and Qt Designer
Basic understanding of Qt tab stop ordering and FreeCAD TechDraw TaskPanel architecture
implementation_steps: Locate the UI definition files corresponding to the Section Plane task panel (e.g., TaskSectionView.ui, TaskComplexSection.ui, or related dialog UI files in src/Mod/TechDraw/Gui/).
Open the UI file in Qt Designer and inspect the `<tabstops>` order using the Tab Order editing tool (or check if tab order is set programmatically in the C++ task panel class).
Rearrange the tab stops into a logical top-down, left-to-right sequence covering all interactive controls (spinboxes, line edits, dropdowns, check boxes, and action buttons).
Ensure any dynamic widgets or sub-widgets embedded at runtime maintain proper `QWidget::setTabOrder` relationships.
Build FreeCAD and open the TechDraw workbench.
Launch the Section Plane tool and verify that pressing Tab and Shift-Tab smoothly transitions focus across all fields in the expected sequential order.
Test with other keyboard shortcuts (Enter/Escape) and ensure accessibility remains intact.

21091.title: Link: On copy, don't preselect App::Link sources
21091.feasibility_reason: The issue describes a clear UI behavior change for copying App::Link objects, labeled as a 'Good first issue' and tagged for a Hackathon. It points to a specific dialog where sources are preselected, and outlines the desired change (only the link should be copied, pointing to the original source).
21091.problem_summary: When copying or duplicating objects containing App::Link instances in FreeCAD, the copy dependency selection dialog pre-selects (checks) the link's source objects by default, which can unintentionally duplicate referenced external objects rather than creating a new link pointing to the original source.
21091.root_cause_hypothesis: The dependency resolution logic used when preparing the copy dialog (such as querying `getOutList()` or dependency graphs in GUI copy commands) treats `App::Link`'s target/source (`LinkedObject`) as a regular dependency and checks all dependencies by default, without distinguishing between structural sub-objects and referenced link targets.
21091.suggested_approach: Adjust the copy/duplicate dialog initialization logic so that objects referenced by `App::Link` (via `LinkedObject` or equivalent link properties) are not checked by default when populating the dependency tree, or teach the dependency pre-selection algorithm to exclude referenced link sources from the initial checked state while still allowing users to manually check them if desired.
prerequisites: Working FreeCAD development environment and build setup (CMake, C++17, Qt6/Qt5)
Familiarity with FreeCAD's document object tree, `App::Link`, and GUI copy/paste/duplicate workflows
implementation_steps: Trace the copy/duplicate command in FreeCAD (e.g. `StdCmdCopy` or duplicate action in `src/Gui/CommandDoc.cpp` and `DlgTreeWidget`) to identify where the dependency list is collected and where item check states are initially set.
Inspect how `App::Link` and its source (`LinkedObject`) are identified among the dependencies of selected objects.

Modify the dependency tree initialization logic so that when an `App::Link` is being copied, its linked source object (`LinkedObject`) is either unchecked by default or not marked as a mandatory dependency.
Ensure that if an assembly or container (such as `App::Part`) contains links and the assembly is copied, the links remain checked while their external link sources remain unchecked by default.
Verify that copying only the link correctly reproduces a link object that still points to the original link source upon paste/duplication.

Test edge cases: copying a link whose source is explicitly also in the initial user selection (in this case the source should remain checked because the user explicitly selected it), nested links, and link groups.

32557.title: Sketcher: Scale default shortcut (Z, P, S) conflicts with Rotate / Polar Transform (Z, P)
32557.feasibility_reason: The issue clearly identifies a keyboard shortcut conflict in the Sketcher workbench. Fixing this requires updating the default shortcut mapping configuration file or registry for the Sketcher workbench tools.
32557.problem_summary: The Sketcher Scale tool default shortcut sequence ('Z, P, S') is unreachable because 'Z, P' is registered to Rotate / Polar Transform, causing the action to trigger before the third keystroke can be registered.
32557.root_cause_hypothesis: Multi-key accelerator sequences in Qt trigger as soon as an exact match is reached. Since 'Z, P' is assigned to Rotate / Polar Transform, pressing 'Z' then 'P' matches that shortcut immediately and consumes the event, preventing the 'Z, P, S' sequence for Scale from ever triggering.
32557.suggested_approach: Update the default keyboard shortcut for the Scale command in Sketcher to avoid prefix collision with other Sketcher commands, resolving any secondary collisions (e.g., if reassigning to 'Z, S', adjust conflicting commands such as Mirror).
prerequisites: Ability to build FreeCAD and the Sketcher module from source.
Understanding of FreeCAD Command registration (sAccel string definition and Qt QKeySequence formatting).
implementation_steps: Search the Sketcher codebase for the 'Z, P, S' string to locate the command definition for the Scale tool (and check definitions for 'Z, P', 'Z, S', etc.).
Inspect existing Sketcher default shortcuts across tools to identify available, non-conflicting key sequences with intuitive mnemonics.

Update the sAccel property (or shortcut definition string) for the Scale command (e.g., to 'Z, S' or another agreed shortcut sequence), adjusting any other transform tools if necessary to maintain consistency without creating new collisions.
Compile the Sketcher module and run FreeCAD.
Open Sketcher, draw geometry, and verify that pressing the configured key sequences triggers Rotate and Scale separately without intercepting each other.
Verify that the updated shortcut appears correctly in the menu, toolbar tooltip, and keyboard shortcut settings.

24440.title: PartDesign: UX could use optimization in order to add elements on some lists
24440.feasibility_reason: The issue requests UX improvements and standard list interactions (Ctrl+A, Ctrl+Click, Shift+Click) as well as continuous selection mode for PartDesign tools like Additive/Subtractive Pipe. While clear in intent, it touches multiple UI task panels and list widgets in the PartDesign workbench, requiring familiarization with Qt item selection models and FreeCAD task panel implementations.
24440.problem_summary: PartDesign Pipe and Loft task dialogs require re-clicking 'Add Edge' or 'Add Section' for each individual item, and the list widgets lack standard multi-selection capabilities (Ctrl+Click, Shift+Click, Ctrl+A).
24440.root_cause_hypothesis: TaskPipeParameters and related PartDesign task panels deactivate selection mode after picking a single element instead of keeping 'Add' mode toggled until explicitly stopped (unlike TaskFillet/TaskChamfer/TaskDressUp). Furthermore, the QListWidget or QTreeWidget controls use default single-selection modes (QAbstractItemView::SingleSelection) and do not handle standard keyboard shortcuts for list manipulation.
24440.suggested_approach: Update TaskPipeParameters (and TaskLoftParameters / auxiliary profile selectors) to enable continuous selection when the 'Add' or 'Remove' buttons are toggled, matching the behavior in TaskDressUp/TaskFillet. Set selection mode to QAbstractItemView::ExtendedSelection on the relevant QListWidget/QTreeWidget views and implement standard shortcuts (such as Ctrl+A to select all and Delete to remove selected items).
prerequisites: Build FreeCAD from source with PartDesign module enabled.
Inspect how TaskDressUpParameters or TaskFilletParameters handles interactive continuous selection and button toggle states via Gui::SelectionObserver.
implementation_steps: Inspect TaskPipeParameters.cpp, TaskPipeOrientation.cpp, and TaskLoftParameters.cpp to see how 'Add' and 'Remove' buttons initiate Gui::SelectionFilter and handle selection callbacks.

Refactor the 'Add Edge' / 'Add Section' button logic so that the button is checkable (toggled) and continuous selection remains active until the user clicks the button again or closes the task dialog, similar to TaskDressUp.

Update the QListWidget / QTreeWidget instances (for spine edges, auxiliary paths, and profile sections) to use QAbstractItemView::ExtendedSelection (or MultiSelection) so users can use Ctrl+Click, Shift+Click, and Ctrl+A.
Enable deletion of multiple selected items at once from the lists when clicking 'Remove' or pressing the Delete / Backspace key.
Ensure 3D viewport highlight / preselection stays synchronized with the selected items in the lists when multiple items are selected.
Test Additive and Subtractive Pipe workflows with single and multi-edge selection, auxiliary profiles, and multiple section additions to verify consistent behavior and prevent regressions.
